summary: Streaming responses disconnecting after Hosted API deploy (SSE stream reset / incomplete chunks)
description:
Issue summary:
Acme AI reports intermittent disconnects on streaming responses (SSE) beginning shortly after a Redwood Hosted API deploy on 2025-02-07/08. Symptoms: stream terminates early (client sees network error / EOF), and the final chunk is missing; retries typically succeed.

Impact:
- Estimated 2.1–3.4% of streaming requests in us-east failing with disconnect/reset during peak (per customer).
- Customer-facing chat UI shows partial answers and then errors.
- Non-streaming requests appear unaffected.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted API, prod, us-east
- Endpoint: POST /v1/chat/completions (stream=true)
- SDK: customer uses node fetch + EventSource parsing (also reproduced with curl)

Customer-provided timeline:
- 2025-02-07 ~19:30 UTC: first observed stream resets
- 2025-02-08 15:40 UTC: customer opens ticket; confirms issue still active

Steps to reproduce (Redwood support reproduction):
1) Run a streaming request with a longer max_tokens (>= 800) and moderate output.
2) Observe occasional early termination with incomplete SSE sequence.

Example request (sanitized):
- x-request-id: req_01HPJ1X9W6Q2M8Z2KJ7A
- tenant: acme-ai-prod
- region: us-east
- model: rw-llama-3-70b-instruct

Observed behavior:
- Client sees: "socket hang up" or "unexpected EOF"
- Server-side logs intermittently show upstream reset / premature close

Notes:
Initial correlation suspected with a deploy to the streaming gateway / edge proxy configuration. We could not quickly confirm deploy context from incident tooling during triage (deploy metadata not surfaced in the incident-bot thread), so investigation relied on release engineer confirmation and manual deploy timeline checks.

Requested outcome:
- Restore stable streaming without requiring client-side workaround.
- Provide a clear RCA / mitigation steps for Acme AI.
- Improve future triage by surfacing deploy context and deep links directly from incident workflows.
comments: 2025-02-08 16:05 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support): Acknowledged. We’re investigating on our side; can you confirm if non-streaming calls (stream=false) are stable? Also, please share a few x-request-id values from failed streams and approximate timestamps (UTC).

2025-02-08 16:18 UTC — Customer (Acme AI): Non-streaming is fine. Streaming fails ~3% with `socket hang up`. Sample request IDs: req_01HPJ1X9W6Q2M8Z2KJ7A (16:11 UTC), req_01HPJ1Y0W1J9A2FQ8K3R (16:12 UTC), req_01HPJ1YB1G4D9A0M7T1C (16:15 UTC). This started after yesterday’s changes on your side (we did not deploy anything).

2025-02-08 16:33 UTC — Dev Patel (Support, assignee): Pulled logs for those request IDs. Seeing intermittent `upstream_reset` from stream-gateway → router around 25–40s into the stream. Not seeing model-side errors. Escalating to on-call SRE + release eng for deploy correlation in us-east.

2025-02-08 16:46 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Confirmed deploy to stream-gateway in us-east started 2025-02-07 19:12 UTC, completed 20:05 UTC. Notably includes changes to response flushing behavior. We’re rolling back stream-gateway in us-east to previous build to test impact.

2025-02-08 17:10 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Update: rollback initiated for stream-gateway in us-east. Expect partial recovery within ~10–15 minutes as pods recycle. We’ll monitor disconnect rate and confirm with you.

2025-02-08 17:34 UTC — Jacob Stein (Diagnostics): Metrics show `stream_disconnect_rate` dropping from ~2.8% to ~0.4% within 10 minutes of rollback. Remaining failures appear to be normal baseline client disconnects. Continuing monitoring for the next hour.

2025-02-08 18:12 UTC — Customer (Acme AI): Confirming improvement from our side. Seeing only sporadic disconnects now (seems back to normal). Please share RCA once available and whether we need to adjust any keepalive settings.

2025-02-09 00:40 UTC — Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Root cause likely the stream-gateway change that altered flush cadence for SSE chunks. Under certain token emission patterns, the proxy buffered longer than expected and hit idle/read timeout thresholds for some client networks. Fix is to revert flush behavior and add explicit periodic keepalive frames for long generations.

2025-02-09 02:15 UTC — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Patch prepared and rolling forward as stream-gateway 2.31.1 with keepalive + timeout guardrails. Rollout starting in us-east canary now; will widen after 30 minutes if stable.

2025-02-09 03:05 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Forward fix deployed (2.31.1) to us-east after stable canary. Disconnect rate holding at baseline (~0.3–0.5%). No customer action required; client-side retries remain recommended best practice for streaming but should no longer be needed for elevated failures.

2025-02-12 19:30 UTC — Dev Patel (Support): Following up with final notes + links. We also filed internal follow-up to improve incident tooling so deploy context and deep links are present immediately during streaming-related incidents.
resolution:
Resolution summary:
- Immediate mitigation: rolled back stream-gateway deployment in prod us-east on 2025-02-08, reducing elevated streaming disconnects to baseline.
- Permanent fix: deployed stream-gateway 2.31.1 on 2025-02-09 with restored SSE flush cadence and periodic keepalive frames for long-running generations; added guardrails to avoid hitting idle/read timeouts.

Root cause:
A deploy regression in the streaming gateway changed SSE chunk flush behavior. In some sessions, responses were buffered longer than intended and tripped timeouts/resets in the edge/proxy layer or intermediate networks, causing client-visible disconnects and incomplete streams.

Customer communication:
- Confirmed non-streaming unaffected.
- Confirmed rollback resolved elevated failures.
- Confirmed forward fix deployed and stable; no customer changes required.

Diagnostics/process improvement:
During initial triage, responders had to manually confirm deploy timing because deploy context was not immediately surfaced in incident tooling. As a follow-up, SRE/Tooling is enhancing incident context gathering to include a “Recent deploys” card and Console deep links (deploy timeline + streaming disconnect dashboards) to reduce future MTTR.

Suggested deep links (internal):
- Console → Deploy timeline (stream-gateway, us-east, last 6h)
- Console → Streaming reliability dashboard (disconnect_rate, reset_by_upstream, p95 stream duration)
- Logs → stream-gateway request-id search with incident time window

Status: Closed after 7 days stable metrics + customer confirmation.
internal_notes:
Internal follow-ups:
- Ensure incident-bot v2 attaches deploy context + direct Console deep links for the service/region/time window (align with incident-context-collection-guidelines).
- Add alert annotation linking streaming disconnect spikes to recent deploy events for stream-gateway.
- Confirm edge timeout configuration is consistent across regions and documented in the streaming runbook.

Data handling:
- No customer prompt/content stored in this ticket. Request IDs and tenant name are operational identifiers only.

On-call handoff note:
If this pattern reoccurs, first check: recent deploys (stream-gateway/api-gateway), then edge/proxy timeout metrics, then saturation/queue signals to rule out backpressure-driven disconnects.
